The React Compiler memoizes components and hooks on its own. In a project that builds with it, `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `memo` are left over from before, and the dependency lists of `useMemo` and `useCallback` are one more thing to keep right by hand. React's docs keep them as an escape hatch for code the compiler can't optimize, so this rule is for a project that has decided not to use them.

It reports `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `memo` imported from `"react"`, under any name, and `React.useMemo` and the like on the default or namespace import. It doesn't run the compiler: it doesn't know whether the compiler actually compiled the component a call is in.

`"use no memo"` or `"use no forget"` at the top of a component or hook tells the compiler to leave that function alone, so the rule leaves the calls in it alone too, and the same directive at the top of a file turns the rule off for the whole file. As for the compiler, the directive counts in a component or a hook: a function declaration named like one, a function that is the whole initializer of a variable named like one, or a function passed to `memo()` or `forwardRef()`, which calls a hook or creates JSX itself, or a function that opts in with `"use memo"`. The compiler doesn't look inside a function it compiles, so the outermost component or hook around a call decides. A directive in a helper function inside a component means nothing to the compiler, and nothing to the rule. `memo(Component)` isn't reported if `Component` itself opts out, or is a class, which the compiler never compiles.

A suggestion removes the call where the rewrite is exact: `useMemo(() => value, deps)` becomes `value` if the arrow has no parameters and no types, `useCallback(fn, deps)` becomes `fn`, and `memo(Component)` becomes `Component` if the compiler would still find it: by a name it looks at, and by a hook call or JSX in it. The suggestion also removes the import once nothing else uses it. It isn't offered where it would drop a comment, or in a function the compiler never finds, like `export default () => ..`, where the call is all the memoization there is. It's a suggestion and not a fix because the compiler can compile a component differently once the manual memoization is gone, which is a change to review. The other shapes, like `memo(Component, arePropsEqual)`, a `useMemo` whose factory has a block body, or a call with type arguments, are reported without a suggestion.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/react-no-manual-memoization" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
import { memo, useCallback, useMemo } from "react";

function Total({ items, onSave }) {
  const total = useMemo(() => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0), [items]);
  const save = useCallback(() => onSave(total), [onSave, total]);
  return <button onClick={save}>{total}</button>;
}

export default memo(Total);
```

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import React from "react";

function Total({ items }) {
  const total = React.useMemo(() => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0), [items]);
  return <span>{total}</span>;
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Total({ items, onSave }) {
  const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0);
  const save = () => onSave(total);
  return <button onClick={save}>{total}</button>;
}

export default Total;
```

A component that opts out of the compiler:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { useMemo } from "react";

function Total({ items }) {
  "use no memo";
  const total = useMemo(() => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0), [items]);
  return <span>{total}</span>;
}
```

`withTotal` isn't a component, so the compiler looks inside it and compiles `Total` on its own. The directive in `withTotal` doesn't cover the call:

{/* bad */}
```jsx
import { useMemo } from "react";

function withTotal(Wrapped) {
  "use no memo";
  const Total = ({ items }) => {
    const total = useMemo(() => items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.price, 0), [items]);
    return <Wrapped total={total} />;
  };
  return Total;
}
```

A `memo` from another module:

{/* good */}
```jsx
import { memo } from "./memo";

export const cached = memo(expensive);
```

## When not to use it

Only with the React Compiler. Without it, `useMemo`, `useCallback` and `memo` are how a component skips work.

The compiler skips a component that breaks the rules of React, and then the manual memoization in it is all it has. Turn on the `react-hooks` rules of the compiler and fix their reports in a component before you remove its memoization. In particular, `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization` reports a `useMemo` or `useCallback` that the compiler can't preserve: it says the compiler isn't memoizing that value the way the code does, so removing the call there changes what the component does.
